design.objective: Remove duplicate desktop page titles and one shell row by placing existing route tabs inside the application header while preserving mobile behavior and all tab operations.
users: Desktop users switching repeatedly among workbench, system, workflow and release-management pages
Phone users retaining the compact sticky header and independent tab row

requirements.statement: Desktop renders route tabs inside the application header without the duplicate breadcrumb or separate tab row.
acceptance: Business content moves upward by the removed row height
requirements.source: User highlighted both regions and confirmed option 1
counterexample: User management remains visible in breadcrumb and tabs

requirements.statement: Project selection, sidebar toggle, inline tabs and global header actions remain simultaneously usable on desktop.
acceptance: Tab overflow does not displace fixed controls
requirements.source: Existing shell workflow and confirmed approach
counterexample: Several tabs hide the account menu or project selector

requirements.statement: Existing tab navigation and context-menu behavior remains unchanged.
acceptance: Switch, close, refresh, close others and close all keep current semantics
counterexample: Moving tabs resets tabsStore or makes dashboard closable

requirements.statement: Phone viewports retain the independent sticky tab row and current-page title.
acceptance: 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 remain usable without page horizontal overflow
counterexample: All phone tabs are compressed into the 56px global header

invariants: tabsStore remains the sole route-tab state source
UiTabs remains responsible for tab commands and context menu
Project context and global account actions remain usable
No page-level horizontal overflow is introduced
constraints: Use existing Vue 3, Element Plus and shell components
Do not add dependencies or modify backend and business pages
Meet desktop and required phone viewport behavior

selected_approach.name: Desktop inline header tabs with mobile independent tabs
selected_approach.reason: Removes repetition and a full desktop shell row while preserving navigation and mobile ergonomics.

alternatives.name: Keep two rows and weaken breadcrumb
alternatives.rejected_because: Retains unnecessary vertical space and partial duplication.

alternatives.name: Remove tabs and keep breadcrumb
alternatives.rejected_because: Removes an established repeated-work navigation capability.

components.name: AppLayout
components.responsibility: Mount UiTabs inline on desktop and below the header on mobile

components.name: UiTabs
components.responsibility: Render and operate the same route tabs in either placement

components.name: shell styles
components.responsibility: Constrain inline width, height, overflow and mobile fallback

interfaces.name: UiTabs props
interfaces.contract: currentPath remains route.fullPath regardless of placement

transitions: choose mutually exclusive desktop or mobile mount
data_flows.output: one authoritative tab strip with unchanged commands

error_handling.condition: Inline tabs exceed available desktop width
error_handling.behavior: Middle region shrinks and uses tab navigation without overlapping fixed controls
error_handling.recovery: Close tabs or use navigation controls

error_handling.behavior: Inline tabs are replaced by the independent sticky tab row

performance: No additional requests or duplicated state
compatibility: Preserve tab commands and required phone viewports
operations: Build, geometry and console checks provide evidence

verification_strategy.signal: Desktop title is not duplicated and fixed controls remain usable
verification_strategy.method: Desktop browser inspection with multiple tabs
Switch, close, refresh and context-menu interactions

verification_strategy.signal: Mobile retains separate tabs without page overflow

verification_strategy.method: npm run build and git diff --check

assumptions.text: Element Plus tab navigation works inside a flex child with min-width zero
assumptions.basis: Existing UiTabs uses Element Plus card tabs and flex sizing
assumptions.falsifier: Browser shows tabs expanding outside the middle region

decisions.decision: Merge tabs into desktop header and preserve an independent mobile tab row
decisions.reason: Removes repetition without harming mobile ergonomics

risks.risk: Three header regions compete for width
risks.mitigation: Fix side controls, shrink middle tabs and verify overflow

risks.risk: Responsive rendering creates duplicate tab instances

approval.evidence: User reviewed the landed design, confirmed it, and explicitly directed implementation.

global_constraints: Do not add dependencies or change backend, route contracts, tabsStore or business pages
Keep project selector and global actions usable
Keep mobile title and independent sticky tabs
Do not introduce page-level horizontal overflow

file_map.responsibility: Responsive shell composition and UiTabs mount location
file_map.evidence: Current template owns header, breadcrumb and independent UiTabs

file_map.responsibility: Header, tabs, breakpoint and overflow layout
file_map.evidence: Current selectors define app-header, breadcrumb, ui-tabs-bar and mobile behavior

tasks.goal: Consolidate desktop route tabs into the application header while preserving mobile and tab behavior.
input_facts: AppLayout currently renders breadcrumb and UiTabs as separate desktop rows
UiTabs owns all route-tab commands and consumes only currentPath plus tabsStore
mobileView is the existing 760px breakpoint signal
AppLayout and styles.css contain unrelated user changes that must be preserved

steps.action: Capture current desktop and mobile DOM and geometry baseline
steps.expected: Desktop contains breadcrumb plus independent tabs; mobile independent tabs remain functional

steps.action: Modify AppLayout to mount UiTabs inline on desktop and independently only on mobile
steps.expected: Exactly one UiTabs is rendered at every viewport

steps.action: Add constrained desktop flex and mobile fallback styles
steps.expected: Header controls do not overlap and content moves upward

steps.action: Run frontend build and focused diff check
steps.command: npm --prefix web run build && git diff --check -- web/src/views/AppLayout.vue web/src/styles.css

steps.action: Verify desktop tab commands and three phone viewports
steps.expected: No duplicate title, behavior regression, console error or page overflow
steps.evidence: Browser interactions, DOM, console and geometry

acceptance_checks: Desktop current title appears only in inline tabs and the separate tab row is absent
Project selector, sidebar toggle, tabs and global actions do not overlap
Switch, close, refresh, close others and close all retain current behavior
375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 keep independent tabs without page overflow
Frontend build and diff check pass
risks: Medium desktop widths may constrain the tab region
Incorrect conditions may render duplicate UiTabs
tasks.rollback: Restore independent UiTabs placement and prior desktop ui-tabs-bar styling without changing tabsStore or business state.
stop_conditions: The change requires tabsStore or route-contract modification
Fixed header controls cannot coexist at supported desktop widths
Mobile page overflow cannot be corrected within the two approved files
escalation_conditions: The confirmed mobile-independent-tabs rule must change
The global navigation architecture requires redesign

integration_checks.command: npm --prefix web run build && git diff --check -- web/src/views/AppLayout.vue web/src/styles.css
integration_checks.expected: TypeScript, Vite and diff checks pass before browser acceptance

approval.evidence: User confirmed the landed design and explicitly requested direct development.

plant_boundary_candidates: UiTabs responsive mount and CSS geometry

assumptions.text: A single UiTabs can move between mutually exclusive responsive mount points without state loss
assumptions.basis: UiTabs state is stored in Pinia, not component-local state except the transient context menu
assumptions.falsifier: Viewport changes reset route tabs or produce duplicate listeners
